Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, and `config.hosts.clear` in `config/environments/production.rb`.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, and Hotwire JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.

## Data Model (Preparing Quizzes)
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
  - Validated and saved atomically via `Question#save_with_option_rows`: skips empty option rows, requires `body`, requires `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`), and requires `>= 1` correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
- `Option` (`question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`).

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`, `Moderate::ExportsController#show`):
  - Renders `Quiz#to_export_json` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
  - `Quiz#as_export_json` writes **only** `"title"` and `"questions"` (`"text"`, `"active"`, `"options"` -> `"text"`, `"correct"`), preserving `questions` and `options` order. Do not include IDs, timestamps, or future game run/response data: export is strictly for moving quiz contents.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`, `Moderate::ImportsController`, `Quiz::Importer`):
  - Validates JSON structure and all quiz/question/option rules upfront and creates the new `Quiz`, `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically inside a single transaction.
  - `active` defaults to `true` when omitted; `correct` defaults to `false` when omitted.
  - Always creates a new `Quiz` even if a quiz with the same `title` already exists, then redirects (`303`) to the newly created quiz page.

## Preview Mode
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview` (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`) steps through `quiz.questions.active.ordered` one at a time using stateless query parameters (`step`, `score`, `picked`, `finished`). No preview answers are persisted to the database, cache, or session.

## Design System Classes Available for Future Releases (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`)
`quizzy.css` already includes component styles for upcoming live game features:
- **Moderator Runs & Responses**: `.runs-table`, `.badge--running`, `.badge--finished`, `.tabs`, `.tab`, `.response-options`, `.response-option`, `.response-card`, `.mark--right`, `.mark--wrong`, `.mark--winner`, `.pager`.
- **Big Screen Presentation (Stage)**: `.cover` (`.cover--blue`, `.cover--night`, `.cover--calm`), `.screen`, `.screen__top`, `.screen__body`, `.screen-controls`, `.lobby`, `.qr`, `.counter-pill`, `.stage-question__num`, `.stage-question__body`, `.stage-options`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader`, `.winner-banner`.
- **Mobile Participant Play**: `.play`, `.join-form`, `.waiting`, `.waiting__gem`, `.play-question__num`, `.play-question__body`, `.play-options`, `.play-option` (`.is-picked`, `.is-correct`), `.play-status` (`.play-status--right`, `.play-status--wrong`), `.result-card`.

module GamePresence
  extend self

  DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL = 5.seconds

  @mutex = Mutex.new
  @connections = {}
  @http_grace = {}

  def connect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
    return false unless game_id && player_id && connection_id

    @mutex.synchronize do
      was_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now_monotonic)
      game_conns = (@connections[game_id] ||= {})
      (game_conns[player_id] ||= Set.new).add(connection_id)
      @http_grace[game_id]&.delete(player_id)
      !was_online
    end
  end

  def disconnect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
    return false unless game_id && player_id && connection_id

    @mutex.synchronize do
      now = now_monotonic
      was_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
      if (game_conns = @connections[game_id])
        if (player_conns = game_conns[player_id])
          player_conns.delete(connection_id)
          game_conns.delete(player_id) if player_conns.empty?
        end
        @connections.delete(game_id) if game_conns.empty?
      end
      now_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
      was_online && !now_online
    end
  end

  def mark_active_http(game_id, player_id, ttl: DEFAULT_HTTP_TTL)
    return false unless game_id && player_id

    @mutex.synchronize do
      return false if @connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?

      now = now_monotonic
      was_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
      (@http_grace[game_id] ||= {})[player_id] = now + ttl.to_f
      !was_online
    end
  end

  def leave(game_id, player_id)
    return false unless game_id && player_id

    @mutex.synchronize do
      now = now_monotonic
      was_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
      @http_grace[game_id]&.delete(player_id)
      now_online = player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
      was_online && !now_online
    end
  end

  def online_player_ids(game_id)
    @mutex.synchronize do
      now = now_monotonic
      ids = Set.new

      if (game_conns = @connections[game_id])
        game_conns.each do |pid, conns|
          ids.add(pid) if conns.any?
        end
      end

      if (grace = @http_grace[game_id])
        grace.delete_if { |_pid, exp| exp <= now }
        grace.each_key { |pid| ids.add(pid) }
        @http_grace.delete(game_id) if grace.empty?
      end

      ids.to_a
    end
  end

  def reset!
    @mutex.synchronize do
      @connections.clear
      @http_grace.clear
    end
  end

  private

  def now_monotonic
    Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  end

  def player_online_locked?(game_id, player_id, now)
    return true if @connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?

    exp = @http_grace.dig(game_id, player_id)
    exp.present? && exp > now
  end
end

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus + Action Cable / Solid Cable) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare` for `primary`, `cache`, `queue`, and `cable`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, `config.hosts.clear`, and `config.action_cable.disable_request_forgery_protection = true` so HTTP and WebSocket (`/cable`) connections work on any host name without SSL.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, `rqrcode` SVG QR generation, and Hotwire + Action Cable JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.
- Player endpoints live under `/play/:code` (`PlaysController`) and require no account.
- Action Cable channels authorize moderator stage subscriptions using a signed `Rails.application.message_verifier("quizzy_stage_token")` token (`StageChannel`) and identify joined players using a signed `quizzy_player_cable_token` (`PlayChannel`).

## Data Model
### Preparing Quizzes
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`, `has_many :games`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
  - Validated and saved atomically via `Question#save_with_option_rows`: skips empty option rows, requires `body`, requires `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`), and requires `>= 1` correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
- `Option` (`question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`).

### Live Games
- `Game` (`quiz_id`, `code`, `status`, `question_ids`, `current_question_index`, `state_version`, `join_base_url`, `started_at`, `ended_at`):
  - `status` transitions monotonically under row locks: `"waiting"` -> `"question_open"` <-> `"question_closed"` -> `"ended"`.
  - `question_ids` snapshots `quiz.questions.active.ordered.pluck(:id)` when starting so inactive questions are skipped and question numbering (`"Question 1 of N"`) stays consistent throughout a game run.
  - `state_version` increments on every state transition for race-free live synchronization.
- `Player` (`game_id`, `name`, `token`):
  - Remembered per game in a persistent signed `httponly` cookie (`quizzy_player_<code>`) so reopening `/play/:code` in the same browser continues as the same player while other games on the same quiz remain independent.
- `Answer` (`game_id`, `player_id`, `question_id`, `option_id`):
  - Unique index on `[game_id, player_id, question_id]`; updated in place while `question_open?` so a player can change their pick until `"Finish"` closes the question (last pick counts).
- `GamePresence`:
  - Thread-safe presence tracker counting active WebSocket subscriptions per `(game_id, player_id)` (with HTTP fallback when WebSockets are unavailable) so `"Players: X"` and `"Answers: Y / X"` accurately reflect players currently in the game.

## Live Synchronization & Answer Confidentiality
- `GameBroadcaster` synchronously broadcasts lightweight state/count signals over Action Cable (`game:<id>:stage` for moderators, `game:<id>:play` for players).
- Stimulus controllers (`stage_controller.js` and `play_controller.js`) combine instant Action Cable push updates with `visibilitychange` and lightweight background state polling + answer POST retry/abort handling for crowded conference Wi-Fi, updating the DOM without full page reloads.
- While a question is open (`question_open?`), player HTML, fragments, JSON responses, and `PlayChannel` payloads never include `Option#correct` or correctness indicators. Correctness (`"Correct!"`, `"Wrong!"`, `"No answer"`) is only rendered on `/play/:code` after `"Finish"` transitions the game to `"question_closed"`.

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`, `Moderate::ExportsController#show`):
  - Renders `Quiz#to_export_json` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
  - Outputs **only** `"title"` and `"questions"` (`"text"`, `"active"`, `"options"` -> `"text"`, `"correct"`), omitting IDs, timestamps, and game/player/answer data.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`, `Moderate::ImportsController`, `Quiz::Importer`):
  - Validates JSON structure and rules upfront and creates `Quiz`, `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically in one transaction.

## Preview Mode
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview` (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`) steps through `quiz.questions.active.ordered` statelessly via query parameters (`step`, `score`, `picked`, `finished`) without persisting data.
EOF

I have implemented the live quiz game feature for both the moderator's big screen and players' phones:

- **Game Data Model & Presence (`Game`, `Player`, `Answer`, `GamePresence`)**:
  - Quizzes can be played multiple times, creating independent `Game` runs with their own join codes (`/play/:code`), players, and answers while skipping inactive questions.
  - Active player presence is tracked in real time via Action Cable (`PlayChannel` / `StageChannel`) with HTTP fallback and `pagehide` cleanup, accurately updating `"Players: X"` in the lobby and `"Answers: Y / X"` during open questions.
- **Moderator Big Screen (`Moderate::GamesController` & `stage_controller.js`)**:
  - Added the `"Start a game"` button on the quiz page (`/moderate/quizzes/:id`), creating a new game and opening its big-screen view inside `/moderate`.
  - Lobby displays the quiz title, full join URL as plain text, inline SVG QR code (`rqrcode`) encoding the same URL, `"Players: <count>"`, and the `"Start"` button.
  - Open question displays progress (`"Question X of Y"`), question text, options, live `"Answers: <answered> / <active>"` counter, and `"Finish"` button.
  - Closed question displays per-option answer counts, marks correct options with `"Correct"`, and provides `"Next"` (or `"End quiz"` on the last active question).
  - Ended game displays `"The quiz is over"`.
- **Player Experience (`PlaysController` & `play_controller.js`)**:
  - Public join link (`/play/:code`) asks for `"Your name"` with `"Join"`, remembers the player per game in a persistent signed cookie, shows `"Hi, <name>!"` before start, allows joining at any point before the end, and blocks joining with `"The quiz is over"` after the end.
  - During open questions, tapping an option submits immediately, marks `"Your answer"`, allows changing picks until closed (last pick counts), and never exposes correctness in HTML or JSON before the question is closed.
  - After `"Finish"`, displays `"Correct!"`, `"Wrong!"`, or `"No answer"`; after `"End quiz"`, displays `"The quiz is over"`.
- **Real-Time & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience**:
  - Synchronizes big screen, counters, and phones live without page reloads via Action Cable (`solid_cable` in production) combined with lightweight state catch-up and retry logic.
